subject: religious-studies
title: Eid, Hanukkah and Passover
welcome_lead: Join the celebrations of Islam and Judaism through three of their biggest festivals.
meta_desc: KS3 Religious Studies adventure on Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha, Hanukkah and Passover.
final_note: You can now describe two Muslim Eids and two major Jewish festivals.

concepts.def: Festival ending the fast of Ramadan.
Muslim festival of sacrifice during Hajj season.
Month of daytime fasting for Muslims.
Jewish festival remembering the Exodus from Egypt.
Special Passover meal with symbolic foods.

walkthroughs.body_html: Eid al-Fitr means 'festival of breaking the fast' — it celebrates the end of Ramadan. Eid al-Adha is the 'festival of sacrifice' during the Hajj season, recalling Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son. Both involve prayers, family meals and gifts.

Hanukkah is a Jewish festival lasting eight nights. It remembers the rededication of the Temple in Jerusalem after a small jug of oil miraculously lasted eight days. Families light a candle each night on a hanukiah (nine-branched menorah).

Passover (Pesach) remembers when God led the Jews out of slavery in Egypt under Moses. Families share a special meal called the Seder, eat unleavened bread (matzah) and tell the Exodus story across the eight (or seven) day festival.

mcqs.q: How do Muslims believe the Quran was revealed?
options: Through the angel Jibril (Gabriel) to Muhammad over 23 years; Muslims believe it is the literal word of God, not Muhammad's own words.
The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.
The ontological argument is the same as the cosmological argument.
Muhammad wrote the Quran based on his own teachings.

mcqs.q: What do Christians mean by resurrection, and how does it differ from reincarnation?
options: Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
The ontological argument is the same as the cosmological argument.

Resurrection is the once-for-all bodily raising to eternal life at the end of time (modelled on Christ's resurrection); reincarnation is the soul's repeated rebirth into new bodies. They are distinct doctrines from different religious traditions.
Resurrection and reincarnation are basically the same idea of life after death.

mcqs.q: What is distinctive about the ontological argument?
options: It tries to prove God's existence purely from the concept of God — a priori reasoning needing no empirical evidence about the world.
The ontological argument is the same as the cosmological argument.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
The ontological argument uses scientific evidence to prove God exists.
